translation_en: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah sent cavalry toward Najd. They returned with a man from Banu Hanifah, Thumamah ibn Uthal, chief of the people of Yamamah. They tied him to one of the mosque's pillars. The Messenger of Allah came out to him and asked: What do you have to say, Thumamah? He replied: I have good to offer, Muhammad. If you kill me, you will kill a man whose blood will be avenged; if you show me favor, you will show favor to a grateful man; and if you want wealth, ask for whatever you wish and it will be given. The Messenger of Allah left him until the next day and asked: What do you have to say, Thumamah? He replied: What I told you: if you show me favor, you will show favor to a grateful man; if you kill me, you will kill a man whose blood will be avenged; and if you want wealth, ask for whatever you wish. The Messenger of Allah left him until the following day and asked again: What do you have to say, Thumamah? He replied: I have what I told you: if you show me favor, you will show favor to a grateful man; if you kill me, you will kill a man whose blood will be avenged; and if you want wealth, ask for whatever you wish. The Messenger of Allah said: Release Thumamah. He went to some palm trees near the mosque, bathed, then entered the mosque and said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Muhammad, by Allah, there was no face on earth more hateful to me than yours, but now your face is the dearest of all faces to me. By Allah, no religion was more hateful to me than yours, but now your religion is the dearest of all religions to me. By Allah, no land was more hateful to me than yours, but now your land is the dearest of all lands to me. Your cavalry captured me while I intended to perform 'umrah. What do you advise? The Messenger of Allah gave him good news and instructed him to perform 'umrah. When he arrived in Makkah, someone asked whether he had abandoned his religion. He said: No, I have submitted with the Messenger of Allah. By Allah, not a grain of wheat from Yamamah will reach you unless the Messenger of Allah permits it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi narrated to me, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah sent cavalry toward the land of Najd. They returned with a man called Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi, chief of the people of Yamamah. He related a hadith like al-Layth's, except that Thumamah said: If you kill me, you will kill a man whose blood will be avenged.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While we were in the mosque, the Messenger of Allah came out to us and said: Go to the Jews. We went with him until we reached them. The Messenger of Allah stood and called to them: O community of Jews, accept Islam and be safe. They said: You have conveyed the message, Abu al-Qasim. The Messenger of Allah said: That is what I want: accept Islam and be safe. They again said: You have conveyed the message, Abu al-Qasim. He said the same once more, then said: Know that the land belongs to Allah and His Messenger, and I intend to expel you from this land. Whoever among you has property, let him sell it; otherwise, know that the land belongs to Allah and His Messenger.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me. Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ishaq said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah expelled Banu al-Nadir and allowed Qurayzah to remain and treated them leniently, until Qurayzah later fought. He then killed their fighting men and divided their women, children, and property among the Muslims. Some of them joined the Messenger of Allah, who granted them safety, and they accepted Islam. The Messenger of Allah expelled all the Jews of Madinah: Banu Qaynuqa', who were the people of 'Abdullah ibn Salam, the Jews of Banu Harithah, and every Jew who was in Madinah.
Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Hafs ibn Maysarah informed me, from Musa, with this chain and this hadith. Ibn Jurayj's report is longer and more complete.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi'—the wording is his—narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah say: I will surely expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I leave no one there but a Muslim.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us. Another chain: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil, Ibn 'Ubaydullah, narrated to us. Both reported from Abu al-Zubayr with this chain, with the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; their wordings are close. Abu Bakr said: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah. The other two said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf say: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: The people of Qurayzah surrendered to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. The Messenger of Allah sent for Sa'd, who came to him riding a donkey. When he came near the mosque, the Messenger of Allah said to the Ansar: Stand for your leader—or your best man. Then he said: These people have surrendered to your judgment. Sa'd said: Their fighting men are to be killed and their offspring taken captive. The Prophet said: You have judged according to Allah's judgment—or he may have said: the judgment of the King. Ibn al-Muthanna did not mention the wording perhaps he said, You have judged according to the judgment of the King.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, with this chain. In his report the Messenger of Allah said: You have judged them according to Allah's judgment. Another time he said: You have judged according to the judgment of the King.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani both reported from Ibn Numayr. Ibn al-'Ala' said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: Sa'd was wounded on the day of the Trench by a Qurayshi man called Ibn al-'Ariqah, who struck him in the main artery of his arm. The Messenger of Allah set up a tent for him in the mosque so he could visit him nearby. When the Messenger of Allah returned from the Trench, he put down his weapons and bathed. Gabriel came to him, shaking dust from his head, and said: You have put down your weapons? By Allah, we have not put them down. Go out to them. The Messenger of Allah asked: Where? Gabriel pointed toward Banu Qurayzah. The Messenger of Allah fought them until they surrendered to his judgment. He referred their case to Sa'd, who said: I judge that their fighting men be killed, their women and children taken captive, and their property divided.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us. He said: My father told me that the Messenger of Allah said: You have judged them according to the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Exalted.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham. My father informed me, from 'A'ishah, that Sa'd said, when his wound had begun to heal: O Allah, You know that there is no people I would rather fight for Your sake than those who denied Your Messenger and drove him out. O Allah, if anything remains of the war against Quraysh, keep me alive so I may fight them for Your sake. O Allah, I think You have ended the war between us and them; if You have ended it, let this wound burst open and make my death occur through it. It burst open at his chest. They were startled—there was a tent belonging to Banu Ghifar with him in the mosque—when blood flowed toward them. They said: People of the tent, what is this coming from your side? They found that Sa'd's wound was pouring blood, and he died from it.

'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Sulayman al-Kufi narrated to me: 'Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham, with this chain and something similar, except that it says: It burst open during the night and continued to bleed until he died. It adds that the poet said: O Sa'd, Sa'd of Banu Mu'adh, what became of Qurayzah and al-Nadir? By your life, Sa'd of Banu Mu'adh was steadfast on the morning they departed. You left your cooking pot with nothing in it, while the people's pot was boiling over. The noble Abu Hubab said: Stay, Qaynuqa', and do not depart. They had been heavy burdens in their land, just as rocks weighed heavily at Maytan.

'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma' al-Duba'i narrated to me: Juwayriyah ibn Asma' narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah, who said: On the day the Messenger of Allah returned from the Confederates, he called out among us: No one should pray the noon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah. Some feared the prayer time would pass, so they prayed before reaching Banu Qurayzah. Others said: We will pray only where the Messenger of Allah ordered us, even if the time passes. He did not reproach either group.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Emigrants came from Makkah to Madinah, they arrived with nothing in their hands. The Ansar owned land and property, and they shared with them by giving them half the produce of their property each year, while the Emigrants did the work and upkeep. Anas ibn Malik's mother, Umm Anas—who was also the mother of 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, Anas's maternal half-brother—gave the Messenger of Allah some of her date palms. The Messenger of Allah gave them to Umm Ayman, his freedwoman and the mother of Usamah ibn Zayd. Ibn Shihab said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that when the Messenger of Allah finished fighting the people of Khaybar and returned to Madinah, the Emigrants returned to the Ansar the gifts of produce they had given them. The Messenger of Allah returned my mother's date palms to her and gave Umm Ayman a garden of his in their place. Ibn Shihab said: Umm Ayman, mother of Usamah ibn Zayd, had been a young enslaved woman belonging to 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and was from Abyssinia. When Aminah gave birth to the Messenger of Allah after his father had died, Umm Ayman cared for him until he grew up. The Messenger of Allah then freed her and married her to Zayd ibn Harithah. She died five months after the Messenger of Allah died.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Hamid ibn 'Umar al-Bakrawi, and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qaysi all reported from al-Mu'tamir. The wording is Ibn Abi Shaybah's. He said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from his father, from Anas: A man used to give the Prophet some date palms from his land. This continued until Qurayzah and al-Nadir were conquered, after which the Prophet began returning what the man had given him. Anas said: My family instructed me to go to the Prophet and ask him for what his family had given him, or some of it. Allah's Prophet had given it to Umm Ayman. I went to the Prophet, and he gave them to me. Umm Ayman came, put the cloth around my neck, and said: By Allah, we will not give them to you; he gave them to me. The Prophet said: Umm Ayman, leave them, and I will give you such and such. She said: No, by the One besides whom there is no god. He kept offering until he gave her ten times as many, or nearly ten times as many.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Sulayman, Ibn al-Mughirah, narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: On the day of Khaybar I found a bag of fat. I clutched it and said: Today I will not give anyone any of this. Then I turned and saw the Messenger of Allah smiling.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar al-'Abdi narrated to us: Bahz ibn Asad narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to me. He said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Mughaffal say: On the day of Khaybar, a bag containing food and fat was thrown to us. I jumped to take it, then turned and saw the Messenger of Allah, and I felt embarrassed before him.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated this to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us with this chain, except that he said a bag of fat and did not mention the food.
